metrics.limits: Small, author-created English holdout. Training and holdout share a fictional task; no external, multilingual, clinical, or educational-outcome validation.

predictions.text: Positive results can include people without the condition, so I compare true positives with all positives.
If a condition is rare, the large healthy group can create lots of false positives.
A positive screening result is not a diagnosis because the test sometimes flags non cases.
A negative result is not certain because false negatives can occur.
How common the condition is affects the proportion of real cases among positive results.
Sensitivity measures detected cases rather than the probability of disease among positives.
If someone screens positive they must have the condition for sure.
A negative result is an absolute guarantee of no disease.
The screen confirms the disease with complete certainty.
Positive means definitely ill and negative means definitely well.
Every positive result is conclusive proof of disease.
It is impossible for somebody with a negative screen to be ill.
The test detects ninety percent of cases, therefore ninety percent of positive people are sick.
I think sensitivity is the chance a positive test is a real case.
The ninety percent sensitivity is also the positive predictive value.
Specificity is how likely somebody is to have the condition given a positive.
Sensitivity means the proportion with disease in the positive group.
Ninety percent case detection tells us nine out of ten positives have disease.
The disease frequency is irrelevant to interpreting a positive test.
I can leave prevalence out because sensitivity and specificity are enough.
It makes no difference if the disease is uncommon or widespread.
The same test means the same probability in any group.
The base rate does not affect the fraction of true positives.
There is no reason to consider how common the condition is.
Because false positives occur, screening should never be used at all.
A screening test that misses a case is entirely worthless.
False alarms mean the test has zero value.
An imperfect test is always a waste of effort.
Any false result proves screening is pointless.
If tests are not perfect there cannot be any screening benefit.
